screens.title: What You Type May Be Kept

aiTutor.recap: Treat a chatbot like a stranger's notebook: do not write private things in it.

glossary.definition: Information that could harm you or others if it spread: passwords, codes, ID and card numbers, addresses, medical details and private messages.

paragraphs: When you type into an AI chatbot, your words go to a company's computers. Depending on the tool and its settings, they may be stored, read by staff, or used to improve the system. You usually cannot take them back.
So the safe rule is to type only what you would be comfortable sharing with a stranger. That keeps you safe even if you are not sure how a tool handles your data.
Safe use is also about honesty and judgement: telling people when AI helped, and not letting it make serious decisions for you.

aiTutor.explain: Decide whether each statement is true or false.

widgetData.instruction: Is each statement true or false?

cards.statement: It is fine to paste your banking password so the chatbot can help you log in.
cards.explanation: Passwords, PINs and OTPs are for you alone. No chatbot needs them to help, and sharing one is a risk.
cards.bonusFact: If you ever typed a password or code by mistake, change it straight away.

cards.statement: You can ask for help writing a CV without including your ID number, home address or bank details.
cards.explanation: Useful help rarely needs private identifiers. You can add them later in your own document.
cards.bonusFact: Write the CV with placeholders, then add your own details in your own copy.

cards.statement: A friend's private message is safe to paste in, because it is only a chat.
cards.explanation: Other people's private details are not yours to share. Remove names and personal details first.
cards.bonusFact: Remove names and personal details before you paste, or describe the situation in your own words.

cards.statement: Your employer's confidential files are fine to paste in if the chatbot is free.
cards.explanation: Being free does not make it private. Check your workplace rules before putting work documents into any tool.
cards.bonusFact: Read your workplace's rules, or ask your manager, before you paste work files into any AI tool.

aiTutor.explain: Think about which version still lets the chatbot help, without any private identifiers.

widgetData.question: You want help writing a complaint to your landlord. Which prompt is the safest?

options.text: "My name is [full name], ID [number], I live at [full address]. Write a complaint about the broken water pipe."
"Write a polite, firm complaint to my landlord about a broken water pipe that has not been fixed for two weeks. Leave the names blank."
"Here is my tenancy agreement with all my details. Write a complaint."

widgetData.explanation: It gives the tool everything it needs and leaves the names and details out. You can fill them in afterwards on your own copy.
widgetData.bonusFact: Using placeholders such as [Name] is an easy habit that keeps private details out of the chat.

nodes.label: Protect
nodes.title: Protect private data
nodes.definition: Never type passwords, OTPs, PINs, card or ID numbers. Leave out other people's private details. Use placeholders for names.
nodes.bonusFact: If you ever typed a secret by mistake, change it straight away.

nodes.label: Check
nodes.title: Check before you act
nodes.definition: Verify important facts, and do not let a chatbot make decisions about health, law or money alone. Look at the tool's privacy settings and choose the most private option available.
nodes.bonusFact: Settings differ between tools, so look at yours rather than assuming.

nodes.label: Be honest
nodes.title: Be honest about using it
nodes.definition: If a school, employer or client expects your own work, follow their rules and say when AI helped. Do not pass off a chatbot's text as something you wrote when that is not allowed.
nodes.bonusFact: Your own thinking is the part of the work that cannot be copied, so keep doing it.

widgetData.completionMessage: You have the three safety habits: protect, check and be honest.
widgetData.completionBonusFact: These same habits protect you whichever AI tool you use.
